example.title: Melan Arch Bridge (Reinforced Concrete Bridge), moved from Dry Run Creek to Emma Slater Park

brief: One of the first reinforced-concrete bridges in the United States (1893): a very flat 30 ft Melan-system arch, rising only 3 ft, 6 in thick at the crown with five embedded 4-inch I-beam ribs, on a 16 ft roadway. Spandrel and wing walls are faced with rock-faced reddish quartzite ashlar; square quartzite end posts carry a two-line gas-pipe hand rail. Later moved into a town park and grassed over. For the Kessler street the model keeps the stone-faced spandrels, pipe rail and stone posts on a paved deck with curbs.

names.plate: cast plaque: 1893 · E. R. HOLLOWAY, CONTRACTOR · KESSLER
